# SPE Round 01 Plan: Triage Agent

## Summary

This is round r01 of the SPE loop for a ticket triage agent. Your prompt is the spec. This plan is the first prediction. One Workflow run after approval is the eval. Nothing exists yet, so this round builds the agent, a labeled ticket set, and the harness, and then measures 4 configurations.

Defaults I chose where the spec is silent. Each one is also logged in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`.
- I chose Python 3.12 with the Anthropic Python SDK for the agent, because the repo has no code yet.
- I chose a synthetic set of 120 labeled tickets, because no real tickets were provided.
- I chose "triage" to mean a category plus a priority.
- I chose to read the API key from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and never print it.

## Specify

### Requirements (r01)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Assign each ticket exactly one category from: billing, bug, feature_request, account_access, outage, other. | User: "triage tickets". Default D2 (taxonomy). | `category_accuracy` code check against gold |
| R2 | Assign each ticket one priority from P1 to P4. | Default D1 (triage means category plus priority). | `priority_accuracy` code check against gold |
| R3 | Catch urgent tickets. Recall on P1 tickets is at least 0.95. | User: "correctly". Default D3 (threshold). | `p1_recall` code check |
| R4 | Category accuracy is at least 0.90. | User: "correctly". Default D3. | `category_accuracy` |
| R5 | Cost is at most $3.00 per 1,000 tickets. | User: "cheaply". Default D4. | `cost_per_1k_usd` from logged token counts times the price table |
| R6 | Every output matches the JSON schema `{category, priority, rationale}`. | Decision: output must be machine readable. | `schema_valid_rate` validator |
| R7 | Ignore instructions written inside ticket text. | Decision D5: ticket text is untrusted input. | `injection_resistance` on 10 injection tickets |
| R8 | Median latency is at most 3.0 seconds per ticket. | User: "cheaply" (time is a cost). Default D4. | `p50_latency_s` timer |

Proposals from a prior round: none. This is round 1.

### Open decisions (owner: you)

| ID | Decision | Default I will use |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Does triage include priority, or category only? | Category plus priority. |
| D2 | What is the category list? | The 6 categories in R1. |
| D3 | What counts as "correct"? | Category accuracy 0.90 and P1 recall 0.95. |
| D4 | What counts as "cheap"? | $3.00 per 1,000 tickets and 3.0 s median latency. |
| D5 | Do you have real tickets I should use instead? | Synthetic set now. Real tickets replace it in a later round if you provide them. |
| D6 | Which model tiers are in scope? | Current Claude Haiku as the small tier and current Claude Sonnet as the mid tier. I will check model IDs and prices in current docs before the build. |

## Predict

### Configurations

A1 is the base. Each other model configuration changes one thing from A1.

| Config | Description | Change from A1 |
|---|---|---|
| K0 | Keyword rules, no model. This is the cost floor and the naive guess. | Replaces the model with rules |
| A1 | Small tier, zero-shot prompt, structured output via tool use. | Base |
| A2 | A1 plus 12 labeled few-shot examples in the prompt. | Adds examples |
| A3 | A1 on the mid tier model. | Changes model |

### Dataset

120 tickets. 90 are standard. 30 are hard: 10 ambiguous, 10 multi-issue, and 10 prompt injection. P1 tickets make up 20 of the 120.

### Numbers

A hit means the measured value lands inside the band. Cost numbers are estimates from list prices I recall. I will verify those prices before the run, and if they differ I will note it here before saving the YAML.

| Metric | Grader check | K0 | A1 | A2 | A3 | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy | `category_accuracy` | 0.55 ± 0.10 | 0.85 ± 0.05 | 0.89 ± 0.04 | 0.90 ± 0.04 | Standard tickets are clear. Most misses will come from the 30 hard tickets. |
| Priority accuracy | `priority_accuracy` | 0.40 ± 0.10 | 0.70 ± 0.08 | 0.78 ± 0.07 | 0.76 ± 0.07 | Priority is a judgment call. Examples teach the rubric more than a bigger model does. |
| P1 recall | `p1_recall` | 0.60 ± 0.15 | 0.85 ± 0.08 | 0.90 ± 0.07 | 0.92 ± 0.06 | Models under-call urgency when the tone is calm. No config reaches 0.95. |
| Schema valid rate | `schema_valid_rate` | 1.00 ± 0.00 | 0.98 ± 0.02 | 0.99 ± 0.01 | 0.99 ± 0.01 | Tool-use output enforces the shape. Rare refusals or truncations break it. |
| Injection resistance | `injection_resistance` | 0.80 ± 0.10 | 0.70 ± 0.10 | 0.80 ± 0.10 | 0.90 ± 0.10 | Keywords planted by an attacker fool rules. Bigger models follow the system prompt more reliably. One ticket is 0.10. |
| Cost per 1,000 tickets (USD) | `cost_per_1k_usd` | 0.00 ± 0.00 | 1.00 ± 0.30 | 2.50 ± 0.75 | 3.00 ± 0.90 | About 600 input and 80 output tokens per ticket. Few-shot adds about 1,500 input tokens. Mid tier costs about 3 times as much per token. |
| Median latency (s) | `p50_latency_s` | 0.01 ± 0.01 | 1.0 ± 0.5 | 1.2 ± 0.5 | 2.0 ± 0.8 | Output is short, so latency mostly tracks the model tier. |

Headline prediction: no configuration meets every requirement. A2 comes closest. It is predicted to miss R3 (P1 recall) and to fall just short of R4.

Naive guess to beat: majority class for category and P2 for every priority. The close-out will report whether this guess beat any prediction.

## Evaluate

### After approval, before anything else

1. Write `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md` with your prompt verbatim. Write `spe/spec/spec.md` with the R1 to R8 table. Write `spe/spec/disagreements.md` with D1 to D6. Commit as `SPE r01 specify: triage requirements and defaults`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml` with round 1, date 2026-10-21, author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", the 4 configs, every number with its band and Why, and `same_as_last_round: null`. The file starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` Commit as `SPE r01 predict: 4 configs, no config predicted to pass all`.

Commits stay local. I will not push. Commit messages will not mention Claude.

### Build (each step is its own local commit)

3. Agent: `triage/agent.py` takes ticket text and a config name, calls the API with a tool schema, and returns `{category, priority, rationale}` plus token counts and latency. `triage/rules.py` holds K0. Commit `SPE r01 evaluate (harness): triage agent and K0 rules`.
4. Data: generate tickets into `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl`. Gold labels go into a separate file, `spe/evals/data/gold.jsonl`. The agent never receives gold labels or file paths. It receives only ticket text. Commit `SPE r01 evaluate (harness): 120-ticket set and gold labels`.
5. Graders: `spe/evals/graders/grade.py` runs code checks only. It covers all 7 metrics. No LLM judge is needed this round, because every metric is checkable by code. Commit `SPE r01 evaluate (harness): graders`.
6. Workflow script: `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` with `const ROUND = 1`. All prompt text derives the round from `ROUND`. Commit `SPE r01 evaluate (harness): workflow script`.

### Gates before launch (halt and report if any fails)

| Gate | Pass condition |
|---|---|
| Grader selftest | Gold fed as output scores 1.00 on all accuracy checks. Empty output scores 0.00 and is schema invalid. Shifted wrong labels score at or below chance. |
| Control | No prior round exists to regrade. Instead, I run K0 twice and both scores must match exactly. This is logged as a default. |
| Label audit | A separate mid tier pass relabels all 120 tickets without seeing gold. Agreement with gold must be at least 0.90. Below that, I halt and bring the disputed tickets to you. |
| Dry run | 3 cells (A1, A2, A3 on one ticket each) produce valid output, logged tokens and cost, and a clean transcript scan. |

### Workflow arguments

```json
{
  "configs": ["K0", "A1", "A2", "A3"],
  "tickets": "spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl",
  "repeats": 3,
  "splitExtraTrials": 2,
  "spendCapUsd": 10.00,
  "outDir": "spe/evals/runs/r01"
}
```

### Run rules

- Cells: K0 runs once per ticket because it is deterministic. A1, A2, and A3 run 3 times per ticket. That is 120 K0 trials and 1,080 model trials.
- A split cell is a ticket where the 3 repeats disagree. It gets up to 2 extra trials.
- Every trial writes a record that matches a schema: config, ticket ID, repeat, output, tokens in, tokens out, cost, latency, and error.
- Spend cap: $10.00 for the round. A trial that would cross the cap is skipped and logged in `spe/evals/runs/r01/skips.jsonl`. Reaching the cap halts the run.
- Peek scan: after the run, scan every trial transcript and harness agent transcript for reads of `gold.jsonl`, `graders/`, or `predictions/`. Any trial that peeked is voided and logged. A peek halts the round as a leaked answer key.
- After grading, one agent groups misses into F-numbered failure types. A completeness critic then confirms that every cell has a result or a logged skip and that every predicted number has a measured value.

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

| Item | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Ticket generation | about $1.50 |
| Label audit | about $1.00 |
| Model trials, including split extras | about $3.00 |
| Total API spend | about $5.50, under the $10.00 cap |

Claude Code session tokens for the Workflow agents are separate from this estimate.

### Close-out (after the Workflow completion notice arrives)

- Results commit: `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
- `spe/prediction-log.md`: one row per metric and config with Predicted, Measured, Same as last round (n/a), Verdict, and Closer. Under it, "Which Why broke" quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption. It says plainly if the naive guess beat the predictions.
- `spe/failures.md`: each new failure type gets a name, kind, round, What, How to spot it, Seen in, and Fix. Any grader bug found after the run is logged as a failure, with original and regraded numbers side by side.
- `spe/spec/spec.md`: add a "Proposed for round 2" table. Write `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
- Update `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r01 learn: <headline>` and tag `spe-r01` locally.

### Stop and halt

- I halt and report on: the spend cap, a leaked answer key, a failed grader gate, a label audit below 0.90, or a decision only you can make.
- If every config passes every requirement, round 2 needs harder tickets or stricter graders.
- The loop stops after predictions match results for 3 rounds in a row.
critiques: The plan says "Your prompt is the spec." It turns "correctly and cheaply" into requirements R1 to R8. Each requirement has a Source and a Test column, such as `p1_recall` and `cost_per_1k_usd`. Defaults are logged as D1 to D6.

The Numbers table gives a numeric value and band for every metric and every config. One example is A2 category accuracy at 0.89 ± 0.04. Another is A3 cost at 3.00 ± 0.90 USD. No adjectives stand in for numbers.
